app.name: Node64
app.tagline: Health checks, DynDNS and more in your own network

setup.title: Welcome to Node64
setup.intro: Choose your language and create the local administrator. There is no default password.
setup.password_hint: At least 10 characters. Use a passphrase or a password manager.
setup.agent_name_hint: For example “Pi in the basement”. Shown later in the ipv64 portal, too.
setup.location_hint: For example Home, Office, Parents. A location can have several nodes.
setup.done: The node is set up. You can sign in now.

login.title: Sign in
login.ratelimited: Too many attempts. Please try again in {seconds} seconds.
login.totp_hint: Enter the code from your authenticator app or a recovery code.
login.totp_failed: The code is wrong or expired.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.no_modules: No module is active yet. Enable Healthchecks in the settings.
dashboard.not_linked: Not linked. The node runs standalone.

settings.appearance_hint: Applies immediately, for this browser. Everything scales along, on phones and tablets too.
settings.title: Settings
settings.modules_hint: A disabled module does not run, uses no resources and has no menu entry. Its configuration is kept.
settings.password_changed: Password changed. Other sessions were signed out.
settings.log_level_hint: Debug shows request details, DNS resolution and timings. Secrets stay masked.
settings.updates_hint: Only fetches a version file from ipv64.net, no data is sent.

errors.title: Error
errors.csrf: The form has expired. Please reload the page and submit again.
errors.internal: Internal error. Details are in the log.
errors.password_short: The password needs at least 10 characters.
errors.username_invalid: The username may only contain letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore (3 to 64 characters).

sources.title: Measuring points
sources.stale_hint: No measurement from this point for a while (node offline or location changed).

diag.inside: Down inside, OK outside: problem in the home network, on the node or the internal path.
diag.outside: OK inside, down outside: internet uplink, port forwarding, DNS or firewall.
diag.both: Down inside and outside: the service itself is affected.

docker.title: Docker containers
docker.subtitle: checked locally via the Docker socket
docker.unwatched: Not monitored yet – click to add:
docker.target_hint: Name or ID of the container on this host (suggestions from the container list).
docker.host_hint: Empty = default. unix:///var/run/docker.sock or tcp://socket-proxy:2375 (e.g. docker-socket-proxy).
docker.rules: Docker checks run only on this node (not online, not movable). Rating: running = OK; healthcheck “unhealthy”, stopped, paused or restart loop = down. When linked to ipv64 the state is reported and visible in the portal too.

hc.foreign_readonly: Belongs to another node – read-only here
hc.run_remote: Measured by ipv64 or another node; “run now” only works for own checks.

chart.note_raw: Single measurements per measuring point; gaps = down.

group.label: Group
group.hint: Checks with the same group are listed together.

hc.empty: No healthchecks yet. Create the first one.
hc.delete_confirm: Delete check “{name}” with all its data?

owner.online_hint: Checked by ipv64.net only, shown here for reference
owner.other_hint: Belongs to another node of your account, shown here for reference

hc.run_push: Push checks are reported by the service itself.

form.cert_min_days_hint: HTTPS: report down when the certificate expires in fewer days (0 = off). The expiry date is always read.
form.target_hint: URL, hostname, IP or host:port, depending on the type.
form.push_hint: After saving, the service calls the push URL regularly. If the call stays away longer than period plus grace, the check counts as down.
form.parent_hint: If the parent is down, this check does not alert on its own.
form.icmp_hint: Ping in a container needs unprivileged ICMP (ping_group_range) or CAP_NET_RAW.
form.stabilize_hint: Successes in a row until OK again
form.invert_hint: Down counts as OK and vice versa.
form.sources_hint: Online measurements from the ipv64 locations become available after linking with ipv64.net. The settings are stored already and carried over.
form.locations_hint: Multiple locations from account class Supporter. Every online measuring point counts against the class's healthcheck limit, local measurements never do.
form.policy_hint: With several measuring points (node, Nuremberg, Falkenstein) this rule decides when the check counts as down. If only some report a failure, the check is “partially down”.
form.notify_degraded_hint: Only relevant with several measuring points.

push.title: Push URL
push.hint: Call this URL regularly, e.g. from cron. With ?status=down the service reports an outage itself.

maint.title: Maintenance windows
maint.hint: During a maintenance window checks keep running but do not alert. Measurements are marked and do not count against availability.

hc.empty_hint: Push, HTTP(S), keyword, ping, TCP, port and certificate. Everything stays in your network.

policy.majority: … the majority of measuring points report down

body.test: If you can read this, the channel “{channel}” works.

browser.title: Browser notifications
browser.intro: Outages and recoveries appear right in the browser – no e-mail or app needed. Create a channel of type “Browser” (it applies to the selected checks like any channel) and switch it on here in every browser.
browser.insecure: Browsers allow system notifications only via HTTPS or localhost.
browser.denied: The browser blocked notifications for this site (lock icon in the address bar).
browser.unsupported: This browser cannot show system notifications.
browser.inpage: Messages then appear at the bottom right of the open page.
browser.note: Only delivered while a Node64 page is open in this browser (a background tab is enough).

nf.title: Notifications
nf.empty: No channel yet. Create one so outages get reported.
nf.default_hint: Default channels receive alerts from all checks without their own channel selection.
nf.secret_keep: Leave empty to keep the stored secret.
nf.quiet_hint: During this time only checks marked as critical alert.
nf.base_url_hint: For links in messages, e.g. https://node.example.com. Empty = no links.
nf.rate_per_hour: Max. messages per channel and hour
nf.subject: Subject

twofa.title: Two-factor authentication
twofa.hint: Protects the login with an additional code from an authenticator app.
twofa.enabled: Two-factor authentication enabled. Other sessions were signed out.
twofa.code_wrong: The code does not match. Check the device clock and try again.
twofa.step1: Open your authenticator app (e.g. Aegis, 2FAS, Google Authenticator).
twofa.step2: Scan the QR code or type in the secret.
twofa.recovery_hint: Each code works once if the app is unavailable. Store them safely now, they are not shown again.

apikey.title: API keys
apikey.hint: For scripts and automations against the local API. Usage: Authorization: Bearer <key>.
apikey.name: Name, e.g. backup script
apikey.show_once: The key is shown only now:

backup.title: Backup and configuration
backup.hint: The backup contains the whole database including measurements. The export contains only the configuration as JSON.
backup.restore_hint: The node restarts afterwards. The previous database is kept under /data/backups.
backup.restore_confirm: The current database will be replaced and the node restarted. Continue?
backup.restarting: Database accepted, the node is restarting now. Sign in again in a few seconds.
backup.invalid: This is not a Node64 database.
backup.password_short: The password needs at least 8 characters.
backup.import_hint: Checks are matched by token, channels and maintenance windows by name. Nothing is deleted.
backup.invalid_config: This is not a Node64 configuration file.
backup.password_needed: The file is encrypted, please enter the password.
backup.password_wrong: The password does not match the file.

link.title: ipv64 link
link.unavailable: Linking is not available in this installation.
link.local_notifications: Also send my own channels locally while linked
link.local_notifications_hint: Normally ipv64.net sends all notifications so nothing arrives twice. With this option the node additionally sends its own channels itself.
link.unlink_confirm: Unlink? The node keeps running standalone.
link.keep_checks: Keep my checks running at ipv64 as online checks (within the limit)
link.code_intro: Enter this code at ipv64.net. It is valid for 10 minutes.
link.step2: Enter the code, choose location and remote management
link.waiting: Waiting for the code to be entered at ipv64.net …
link.intro: Link this node with your ipv64.net account. Everything keeps working locally; the connection goes outbound from the node, no port needs to be opened.
link.benefit1: See and edit checks in the portal from any device
link.benefit2: Have checks verified from Nuremberg and Falkenstein too (hybrid)
link.benefit3: Notifications via ipv64 mail, SMS and app
link.privacy: Note: after linking, configuration and results of this node are sent to ipv64.net – including targets in your home network.
link.start_failed_hint: The node must reach hc-srv01.ipv64.net and hc-srv02.ipv64.net via HTTPS (port 443): check DNS, firewall and clock.
link.conflicts_hint: The same setting was changed here and at ipv64.net while there was no connection. Decide which version applies – nothing is overwritten silently.
